text:
alex: Heads-up — I opened PR #62540 to add a "hedge-on-demand" routing fallback. When latency spikes we route to a cheaper quantized variant in the same region for a fast short response, then let the caller re-issue for quality if needed. Need runtime + platform + security eyes before we can schedule a canary. https://github.com/redwood-inference/repo/pull/62540 :eyes:

sam: Can you summarize the surface area changed? Which teams need to sign off?

alex: Sure — short summary: modified router policy, added a runtime flag to allow hedging to a lower-accuracy model variant, and a platform config to opt routes in. Also added a new audit event when hedge happens. Files: routing/service.go, runtime/hedge_flag.go, console/route_config.yaml

maria: tagging runtime (cc @jamal) and security for the audit/event bits. Any user-visible config?

alex: Yes — per-route in console: `hedge: { enabled: true, max_latency_ms: 200, fallback_model: "redwood/llama-7b-q4" }`

jamal: runtime notes: hedging uses KV cache invalidation logic so it must preserve prefix cache semantics. Quick glance: the PR introduces `preserve_prefix_cache` bool, we should avoid flipping that by default. Also we need a perf test for 1, 2, 4 concurrent hedged requests.

sam: platform: we need a canary plan + who owns rollback. Proposed: canary 5% region A for 2 hours, monitor latency, hedge-rate, and token-cost delta. If hedge-rate > 15% or cost delta > 10% abort. Who volunteers to steward canary?

alex: I can steward initial canary. Will pair with jamal for runtime metrics and with maria for audit review.

maria: security: I need the new audit event schema and a short threat model note about cross-tenant data exposure. If hedged model is different infra-wise (e.g., dedicated vs shared), we need encryption/KMS check.

alex: Added a doc at the PR top with the event schema and notes. Snippet: ```json
{"event":"hedge_fired","route":"/chat","fallback_model":"redwood/llama-7b-q4","user_id_masked":true}"
```

jamal: perf test idea: run synthetic workload with 2% p99 tail injection, measure end-to-end latency and per-token cost. I'll add a small k6 script to the PR.

sam: Ops question: does this require infra changes (new pool types)? If so we need infra eyes.

alex: No new infra pools — fallback reuses existing quantized pool. We added a knob so platform can opt which pool aliases are eligible. No new machines.

maria: Security ok to start async review. I want a short writeup of why masking is sufficient and how we avoid logging PII in the event payload.

alex: Will add that to the PR description by EOD.

jamal: I'll add the perf script and a quickbench in runtime CI. Expect a small runtime tweak in hedge_flag.go to preserve cache keys.

sam: OK — can someone from infra do a quick read to confirm no infra ops required? @ops on-call or @infra-owners?

alex: @ops-rotation: ping, need a quick OK that this doesn't expand infra footprint.

ci-bot: build #62540 — success; unit tests 214 passed, 3 skipped.

maria: Assuming infra gives a quick nod, I'm fine to proceed with canary once the audit note lands and jamal's perf numbers look safe.

alex: Thanks — plan: add docs + perf script today, request infra eyes, schedule canary tomorrow during the 2–4pm slot. If anyone cannot make that slot please shout now.

sam: I can be on call for merge and rollback during that slot.

jamal: I can monitor runtime metrics and help triage.

maria: I'll do the security check-in and be available for rollback if needed.

alex: Awesome — leaving the PR in async for final signoffs. Ping me in thread if you find anything blocking. :thumbsup:
